solar is good tech, but...

conventional solar panels work because they can clean themselves, they're usually mounted at an angle to catch more sun and as a side-effect this helps prevent debris sticking to the panels. As soon as you mount solar panels flat then you start to experience badly degraded performance due to cell shading from debris, dirt, leaves etc. I've experienced this from mounting panels flat on RVs, there doesn't need to be any traffic or footfall over the panel to drop enough debris to quickly degrade the panel's performance, a thin layer of road film alone will cause significant loss of performance. Road or foot traffic always drops debris, ranging from mud and gravel upwards. A solar road would need sweeping clean every few hours or its performance would rapidly fall to less than a tenth of its rating.

I'm prepared for someone to link me to what I'm missing WRT solar roads and that there's a method for preventing partial cell shading from debris or some sort of solution to the loss of performance associated with cell shading, but it hasn't happened yet. Until that changes I can see solar panels making great roofs, great fences, but very poor roads and paths.
Even though these panels will be very inefficient there is such a vast area that they can cover on the road system that it should balance out.

my point is why would you put the panels under the road and lose >90% of their performance within hours when you could put them around the sides of the road and keep most of the performance for years. There's already a solar fence about a mile long and 3/4 megawatts alongside the Autobahn in Freising, Germany.

interesting to note that despite this fence having a 35 degree angle and the panels being teflon coated they're still having performance issues related to dirt and debris settling on panels and obscuring cells, imagine how much worse it would be with flat horizontal panels!
